gate_reasoning: Stage 2 scores 24% High, 24% Medium, 52% Low across 50 scored claims. The High-confidence core is strong: six audited primary filings (WiseTech ASX, E2open, Trimble, Uber, Full Truck Alliance, C.H. Robinson 10-K) provide solid revenue foundations for the market-player section; Acocella & Caplice (JBL 2023) gives peer-reviewed academic grounding for PP2.4 and PP2.3 structural claims; TIA's April 2025 fraud report and Verisk CargoNet 2024 data provide credible association-level evidence for PP2.1. The Low majority is driven by three structural problems: (1) all Gartner MQ positioning evidence is sourced from vendor press releases announcing their own positions rather than the Gartner report itself; (2) all market-sizing (TMS global market, digital freight brokerage, US TMS) comes exclusively from aggregator research firms (IMARC, Grand View, Precedence, MarketsandMarkets) without primary cross-validation; (3) a significant proportion of pain-point quantitative claims (freight invoice error rates, tender rejection premiums, TMS adoption rates, carrier performance metrics) are sourced from vendor blogs on the vendor blocklist (Highway, TriumphPay, Locus, SONAR) rather than from primary industry studies. Three specific remediation actions are high-priority before final gating: replace the manh.com newsroom URL for Manhattan Associates with its SEC EDGAR 10-K URL (immediate fix, no research needed); locate the underlying McKinsey blind-handoff study for PP2.5; and obtain an independent TMS adoption survey to replace the InMotion Global vendor-commissioned data in PP2.2. The internal inconsistency in Indonesia logistics cost as % of GDP (14.29% vs 24%) must be reconciled in the narrative. The draft is substantively credible and structurally sound; the source gaps are concentrated in market-sizing and vendor-produced statistics, which is recoverable through targeted deep research.
